title: The Most Dangerous Game

teacherSummary.text: Big-game hunter Sanger Rainsford falls overboard near Ship-Trap Island and finds the chateau of General Zaroff, a Russian aristocrat bored with hunting animals who now hunts shipwrecked sailors. Rainsford refuses to join and becomes the prey for three days. He builds traps that kill a servant and a hound, then leaps into the sea. That night he waits in Zaroff's bedroom; they fight, and Rainsford sleeps in Zaroff's bed.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “The world is made up of two classes—the hunters and the huntees” slowly and put it in my own words: On the yacht, Rainsford tells Whitney that the world is made up of two classes, hunters and huntees. Next, craft. I notice the neat two-part division and the made-up joking word "huntees," which makes the hunted sound unimportant. The strongest word is “huntees”: the comic word shows he gives no thought to how the hunted animal feels. Then, effect. What does Rainsford's view of the world show about him at the start? My answer: Rainsford is confident that he will always be the hunter; the story will reverse this by making him Zaroff's prey, so he learns what the "huntees" feel.
